title: Texas's 34th Congressional District election, 2026
description: Texas's 34th Congressional District, stretching along the Gulf Coast from Brownsville to Corpus Christi, is hosting one of the most competitive House races in the country. Incumbent Democrat Vicente Gonzalez, a moderate Blue Dog Coalition co-chair, faces Republican challenger Eric Flores, an Army veteran and former federal prosecutor endorsed by President Trump. The district voted for Trump in 2024 while re-electing Gonzalez by a narrow margin, making it a top GOP target. The race will test the GOP's gains with Hispanic voters in South Texas and the strength of Democratic incumbency in a district rated as a Toss-up by the Cook Political Report.
polling_note: Only one poll was located, conducted by a Republican party committee (NRCC). Independent nonpartisan polling data for this race was not publicly available as of June 2026.

candidates.name: Vicente Gonzalez
candidates.summary: Vicente Gonzalez is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Texas's 34th Congressional District, first elected in 2016. A moderate Democrat and co-chair of the Blue Dog Coalition, he has focused on affordable healthcare, veterans' benefits, and economic development for South Texas. He previously represented the 15th district before redistricting and won re-election in 2024 by a narrow margin in this Republican-trending seat.

candidates.name: Eric Flores
candidates.summary: Eric Flores is the Republican nominee for Texas's 34th Congressional District. A former U.S. Army infantry captain and assistant U.S. attorney, he prosecuted transnational human smuggling and white-collar crime in the Southern District of Texas. He has been endorsed by President Trump and Gov. Greg Abbott, and his campaign emphasizes border security, support for law enforcement and veterans, and U.S. energy independence.

forecast.rationale: This race is a true tossup based on the available data. The only public poll is a single NRCC-commissioned survey from April 2026 showing Eric Flores at 41% and Vicente Gonzalez at 40%, a negligible 1-point gap within any standard margin of error. However, because this is a partisan-sponsored poll and no independent nonpartisan public polling exists, its evidentiary value is limited. Structural factors cut both ways: the district voted for Trump in 2024 yet re-elected Gonzalez narrowly, and Flores has high-profile endorsements (Trump, Abbott) while Gonzalez is a sitting moderate incumbent and Blue Dog co-chair who has demonstrated crossover appeal. With only one partisan poll at this stage and mixed fundamental signals, the race is best characterized as a tossup with high uncertainty, leaning very slightly toward the incumbent by virtue of incumbency and proven ability to hold the seat.
